coaching_dna.why_it_matters: Louis wants to prove he can go the distance — literally. The marathon is the anchor, but he's also looking to lean out, add muscle, and keep his medical clearance bulletproof. This is about feeling capable in the cockpit and crossing a finish line.

coaching_dna.lifestyle_summary: Unknown — will learn over time. Profile shows solid home gym setup and commitment to 4 sessions/week, suggesting disciplined routine.
coaching_dna.injury_summary: No current injuries — avoids jumping, overhead pressing, deep squatting, and deadlifts
coaching_dna.biggest_strength: Excellent home gym setup and realistic time expectations for layover training
coaching_dna.biggest_weakness: Occasional runner building toward a marathon — aerobic base needs significant development
coaching_dna.biggest_opportunity: 14 weeks to marathon day — tight but doable with smart progression and injury prevention focus
coaching_dna.recommended_weekly_training: 4 sessions/week: Training Day 1 easy aerobic run 30-45min Z2, Training Day 2 strength (lower body hinge/lunge bias, upper pull/press, core — no overhead/deep squat/DL), Training Day 3 tempo or interval run 30-40min, Training Day 4 long run building from 60min toward 90-120min — dates assigned when roster uploaded. Layover sessions = short runs or rower intervals if hotel gym available.
coaching_dna.recommended_recovery_strategy: Prioritise sleep on layovers, use rower for low-impact aerobic work when legs are heavy, deload week every 3-4 weeks leading into marathon taper.
coaching_dna.recommended_nutrition_strategy: Fuel the mileage build — don't cut calories aggressively while ramping volume. Focus protein around strength days, carbs around long runs. Fat loss will follow aerobic load if intake is sensible.
coaching_dna.recommended_coaching_style: Give him the plan, the rationale, and the data — then trust him to execute. He's event-driven and has the kit, so keep communication clear and performance-focused.

options.why: You've just come off a brutal night turnaround (02:25 departure, 13:00 landing) and your body is telling you it needs rest. Recovery drives performance — pushing a key 75-min run when exhausted risks injury and undermines the aerobic base we're building toward your October marathon. I've converted today's long run to a 20-min easy walk to keep blood moving without adding training stress. Your next long run (Sunday 27th) stays intact, and you'll be fresher for the strength session Friday.

options.why: If even a walk feels too much right now, take full rest. Your body has been awake through circadian low-points and crossed time zones — sleep and passive recovery are training tools too. This approach banks maximum freshness for Sunday's easy run and Monday's strength work. With 14 weeks to marathon day, one skipped session won't derail progress, but cumulative fatigue from ignoring recovery signals absolutely will. Train around your roster — this is a red-load day for a reason.
